_why: Operator 2026-10-27: "Could the LLM API monitor these processes if something goes wrong in terms of deployment, that it will fix it automatically … or tell the agents what to do?" Deterministic watchers (no model) run from a host timer every 5 minutes (config/systemd/incidents/tradeai-incident-watchers.timer) and open one IncidentRecord@v1 per condition, deduped by a fingerprint that carries the distinguishing token (SHA, job, lane, symbol). An incident auto-resolves when its watcher collected cleanly and the condition is gone; a watcher whose input is unreadable records a collection gap and resolves nothing. Every input is an EXISTING producer's output; the watchers never write another producer's store. Host timer, not n8n (AGENTS.md section 28.14 item 1 and section 23.14: a monitor never depends on the thing it monitors).

deploy_failures._why: deploy_on_main poller: 388 deploy_failed receipts 2026-10-26/27 reached nobody (comms editor fingerprint stripped the SHA).

lane_health._why: research lane health (scripts/research_lane_health.py) and the cron outage watchdog (scripts/cron_outage_watchdog.py, currently enabled:false in its own config; read only when its receipt is fresh).

main_ci._why: Main CI red on the tip of main. Read-only `gh run list` (GET). Fingerprint = head SHA + workflow, so a new red SHA is a new incident and the old one resolves when the tip moves on green.

llm_backlog._why: Postgres llm_deferred_requests via scripts/lib/llm_deferral.queue_summary(); psycopg2/DB unavailable = collection gap, never an incident.

cap_hits._why: Anthropic credit journal fallback rows whose reason is a cap (hash-chained journal, read only).

dirty_checkout._why: Agent work left in the canonical checkout (2026-10-27, rescued by #2231). Dirty for longer than dirty_minutes opens an incident; first-seen is kept in watchers_state.json.
